title: Whipped chain stitch
subtitle: A raised corded line made by lacing a second thread over a chain base
excerpt: Whipped chain stitch is a two-pass technique. First you lay a line of ordinary chain stitch; then a second thread is laced over each link with a whipping motion, without piercing the fabric. The whipping pulls the chain into a rounded, rope-like cord that stands up clearly from the surface.
sourceNotes: Thérèse de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886); Caulfeild & Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).

glossaryTerms.definition: The length of thread currently being stitched with, running from the fabric to the needle.
Passing the thread over or around a stitch or bar without going through the fabric.

content.text: Whipped chain stitch builds a raised line in two stages. The first pass lays a foundation of chain stitch. The second pass uses a
working thread
to
wrap

over each chain link in turn, always in the same direction, without the needle entering the fabric. The whipping draws the links together into a smooth cord. Because only the first pass requires needle penetration, this stitch suits beginners who already know basic chain stitch.
What you need

items.label: Thread
items.value: Two threads: one for the chain base (stranded cotton or pearl cotton), one for whipping (a contrasting or toning colour works well)

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Any stable embroidery fabric; the chain base needs to lie flat before you start whipping

items.label: Needle
items.value: Crewel needle for the chain base; a blunt tapestry needle for the whipping pass so you slide under links without splitting thread

items.label: Hoop
items.value: A hoop helps for the chain pass; optional for the whipping pass

content.text: Working the stitch
Work a line of chain stitch along your design line from A to the end point. Keep the loops a consistent size, roughly 4 to 5 mm each. Fasten the chain thread on the back.
Thread the tapestry needle with the whipping thread. Bring it up through the fabric just beside the top of the first chain link at A, as close to the start as possible.
Slide the needle under the first chain link from right to left (or left to right, choose one direction and keep it throughout). Do not pierce the fabric or the chain thread.
Pull the whipping thread through with moderate tension, enough to round the chain link into a cord but not so tight that it puckers or distorts the fabric below.
Move to the next chain link and repeat the same slide-under motion. Work every link in the same direction until you reach the end of the line.
To finish, take the whipping needle through to the back of the fabric beside the last chain link and fasten the thread there.
Common mistakes

items.symptom: The whipping thread pierces the chain thread and splits it
items.cause: Using a sharp crewel needle for the whipping pass.
items.fix: Switch to a blunt tapestry needle for the whipping pass. It slides under the loops cleanly without splitting strands.

items.symptom: The cord looks uneven with gaps between some whips
items.cause: Inconsistent tension or the needle is occasionally sliding under only part of a chain link.
items.fix: Make sure the needle passes fully under the top bar of each link. Keep tension even by checking that each whip snugs against the previous one before moving on.

content.text: Uses and related stitches
The chain foundation here is the same as
chain stitch
. The whipping technique also appears in
whipped back stitch
and
whipped running stitch
, which use the same lacing principle over different base stitches.
